exposure: maternal characteristics (nulliparity, high education level, birth plan, psychiatric history, antenatal psychological distress, breastfeeding, age, place of birth, marital status)
obstetric characteristics (instrumental or cesarean birth, pregnancy's level of risk, delivery complication)
outcome: experience of disrespectful care (professionals' words, gestures, and attitudes experienced as uncomfortable, shocked, or offended) during childbirth or postpartum stays
cohort: A representative sample of 7332 women who gave birth in metropolitan France, drawn from the Enquete Nationale Perinatale (ENP) 2021 database.
finding: A quarter of women delivering in France reported experiencing disrespectful care during childbirth and/or postpartum stay, with specific maternal and obstetric factors, including instrumental or cesarean birth, identified as determinants.
mod_finding: Women who experienced disrespectful care were more frequently associated with having had an instrumental or cesarean birth.
cross-section timing: 2 months postpartum (when the outcome data was collected)
